title: Probabilistic Signature Inversion: Learning Conditional Distributions from Truncated Signatures
claim: Deterministic methods return a single smooth path, while ours samples a distribution of plausible paths that capture the reference's roughness.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared top legend, reference path overlaid on all curves
description: Two side-by-side line plots show a stochastic path X(t) over t from 0 to 1. A shared legend sits across the top: black for the reference overlay, blue for ours, and brown, green and red for the deterministic baselines Insertion, Legendre and Fourier. In each panel a rough black reference path is drawn on top. The thick blue curve is one draw from the probabilistic method, and several thin pale-blue curves are other draws that spread around the reference. The brown piecewise-linear curve and the smooth green and red curves are single deterministic reconstructions. They follow the overall trend but miss the fine-scale roughness. The left panel has larger amplitude, about -1 to 1. The right panel has a smaller scale, about -0.15 to 0.05. The eye goes first to the blue and black jagged curves against the smooth baselines. Panel captions at the bottom edge are cut off.
caption: Probabilistic and deterministic signature inversion. Thin blue curves show five randomly selected paths from our probabilistic signature inversion method, with one draw highlighted in thick blue; deterministic baselines return one path each.
abstract: The signature transform is a principled feature map for continuous-time paths, valued for its uniqueness and universality. Recovering a path from its truncated signature is, however, structurally ill-posed, because the truncated signature map is not injective. We therefore reframe truncated signature inversion as a probabilistic problem---learning the conditional distribution of a path given its truncated signature---and adopt a signature-conditioned flow matching model as a practical estimator. This formulation elucidates the fundamental difficulty of inversion: posterior-sampling reconstruction error quantifies the irreducible uncertainty remaining after conditioning on a statistic. For Gaussian process families, we derive this error from the tractable posterior under linear-statistics conditioning, obtaining a closed form for log-GBM and numerically tractable formulas for drifted fBM and OU. This oracle error upper-bounds the corresponding error under truncated-signature conditioning, since truncated signatures are more informative than linear statistics. The experimental results are consistent with the theoretical analysis: the learned sampler under linear-statistics conditioning closely matches the theoretically derived posterior in both reconstruction error and distribution, while reconstruction errors decrease under richer truncated-signature conditioning. Moreover, generated paths faithfully recover the conditioning signature and preserve key distributional and temporal structures. Together, these results establish a well-posed probabilistic framework for truncated-signature inversion, with applicability demonstrated on financial data beyond the process families covered by theory. Code is available at https://github.com/Junoh-Kang/ProbSigInv.
